summary: Windows dock reattach + sleep causes NIC metric equalization and conntrack asymmetry blocking on-prem services
description:
Issue summary: Multiple users report loss of connectivity to internal on-prem services (gitlab, k8s API, internal RDP) after laptop sleep + dock detach/reattach. Impact: Productivity blocked for developers and SREs using docked Windows devices; intermittent and not resolved by simple reconnects. This ticket tracks the investigation, diagnostics, and a coordinated mitigation plan.

High level timeline: 2026-03-09 initial user report; 2026-03-10 reproduced on 3 devices; 2026-03-11 firewall logs confirm asymmetric tuple drops; 2026-03-12 test mitigation validated on one machine.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Connect laptop to corporate dock (Ethernet + Wi-Fi enabled)
2. Establish WireGuard to corp and confirm access to internal services (git clone, kubectl)
3. Put laptop to sleep for ~30-120s
4. Wake machine and detach then reattach dock (or hotplug Ethernet)
5. Attempt to access internal services; observe failures (TCP timeouts, TLS handshake errors)
6. Run 'ipconfig /all', 'route print', and collect PCAP on both interfaces
diagnostics_collected: PCAPs (eth0.pcap, wifi0.pcap); ipconfig_output.txt; route_print.txt; netsh_interface_ip.txt; conntrack_dump.txt from edge firewall; firewall log snippets (fw-prod-01); affected host list (SURF-21, DLX-09, MBP-14-test) uploaded to s3://support/INT-314159/
observed_behavior: After wake and dock reattach, Windows' Automatic Metric assignment sets equivalent InterfaceMetric on Ethernet and Wi-Fi. Outgoing SYNs sometimes choose Wi-Fi source IP while the corporate edge expects sessions from the Ethernet IP. Edge conntrack rejects the asymmetric replies, producing TCP_RST and dropped connections. Symptoms: failed git clones with 'TLS handshake timeout', kubectl unable to reach API (connection reset), RDP sessions hang then disconnect.
expected_behavior: On dock attach, the docked Ethernet should receive a lower metric than Wi-Fi, and the system should prefer Ethernet for internal traffic. After sleep/resume sequences, sessions should rebind or failover cleanly without asymmetric routing to the edge firewall.
workaround:
1) Run PowerShell to set static metrics: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" -AutomaticMetric Disabled -InterfaceMetric 10; Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Wi-Fi" -AutomaticMetric Disabled -InterfaceMetric 50
2) Toggle Airplane mode to force interface re-evaluation
3) Reboot machine if above fails
Note: Workaround must be applied per-machine; SCCM automation planned.
investigation_notes:
- Conntrack dumps show established tuples for 10.1.x.x with return packets sourced from a different internal IP (Wi-Fi), causing conntrack mismatch.
- Reproduced on three distinct makes/models: Surface Pro w/ Surface Dock, Dell Latitude w/ WD19, Lenovo ThinkPad w/ USB-C dock.
- Affected NIC drivers: Intel i225-V (v1.0.3), Realtek USB GigE (v10.32).
- Windows builds observed: 10.0.22621.2485 and 10.0.22621.2590. Not all devices have recent KB security patch; kernel network stack differences are hypothesized.
- Edge firewall (fw-prod-01) policy uses strict conntrack tuples; security team confirms asymmetric tuple rejection.
- Admin note: This is not a VPN tunnel failure; WireGuard endpoint remains UP but application-layer TLS fails due to TCP resets.
next_steps:
1) Collect driver versions + Windows build for all affected fleet devices (assigned Marco Silva)
2) Boot one test host into safe NIC driver (rollback) to validate driver as root cause
3) Prepare SCCM/Intune script to set static InterfaceMetric on corp-managed Windows devices and pilot to 50 users
4) Evaluate temporary firewall conntrack relaxation for 10.0.0.0/8 with Security (low preference)
5) If driver or Windows patch is identified, coordinate vendor driver rollout and Windows update schedule
6) Draft communication to impacted teams with workaround steps
